name: ramp-foot-traffic
description: #1206 (agent occupancy on foot — ground-cell reservation): dig a RAMP_WIDTH=3 ramp, then dispatch 6 on-foot employees down it at once. Turns on the new occupancy check via `debug occupancy on` (world.ts's new_game/sandbox start don't thread an agent_occupancy flag yet at this skeleton phase — see world.ts's own TODO(#1206)), then asserts every employee reaches the far end within a bounded tick budget with nobody left stuck. GAP for the implementer/orchestrator: there is no generic per-tick 'no two agents share a ground cell' harness assertion today (no such field in state-schema-definitions.ts/console-api.ts, and neither `expect` nor a scenario step type expresses it) — this file's own assertions (stuckEmployeeCount:0, pendingActionCount:0, employeeCount unchanged) are the closest proxy available without inventing new harness surface, which is out of scope for a scenario-definition-only change. A direct per-tick occupancy assertion, if wanted, is a state-schema/console-api addition for a follow-up issue, not this one.

expect.note: staffed:true (STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION, balance.ts) grants the roster/fleet for free at game-open, including the two driving.excavator drivers and the rock_digger this scenario needs to carve the ramp below.

steps.description: Skeleton phase (#1206): agent_occupancy isn't threaded through new_game/sandbox start yet (world.ts's own TODO), so the primary toggle is this debug command against GameState.agentOccupancyEnabled. Stubbed to throw at this red phase — the implementer wires it to actually flip the flag.

Staffed vehicles come unmanned (#551) — crew rock_digger #3 with driver #4, one of the two driving.excavator-qualified drivers STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION grants, before ordering any excavation work. Mirrors ramp-navigation.json's own crewing step.

Same geometry as ramp-navigation.json: a 10m, RAMP_WIDTH=3-wide corridor running south from (15,15). depth:5 keeps every per-column step within NAV_MAX_SLOPE_RATIO and RAMP_CUT_SLOPE_RATIO (#1151/#1152) — see that file's own note for the full derivation. Ordering only queues dig_ramp_segment work; the crewed rock_digger below carves it over the following ticks.
Drain every queued dig_ramp_segment layer — the crewed rock_digger (vehicle #3, driver #4) clears one bench at a time until the whole corridor is carved end to end and walkable.

expect.note: Ramp fully dug: every dig_ramp_segment layer landed.
HIRING_COSTS.surveyor = 1200 (balance.ts). Lands as employee #6, alongside staffed:true's roster of 5 (ids 1-5).
Employee #7. With #4 driving the rock_digger, employees 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 (six on foot, more than RAMP_WIDTH=3) are the crew dispatched down the ramp together below.

steps.description: Dispatch six on-foot employees (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 — every hired employee except #4, still crewing the rock_digger) to the ramp's far end all at once, converging into the 3-wide corridor together. No UI control drives `employee dispatch` (same class as ramp-navigation.json's own use of it) — a test hook by design.

All six dispatched walks are the only PendingActions targeting these employees, and dig work already drained to 0 above — pendingActionCount reaching 0 again means every one of the six actually arrived at (15,24) and did its token work, not merely that none is currently flagged stuck. Generous 300-tick budget: six agents funnelling through a 3-wide corridor under the new occupancy check must queue for a cell rather than deadlock, but must still all finish.

expect.note: Every dispatched employee reached the far side: no permanent deadlock in the corridor, nobody abandoned/removed, and the roster count is unchanged from the two hires above.

steps.description: Inspect the ramp's own far end — proves the column is carved (walkable), not just that the employees report unstuck.
